paper.title: Tracking vortex surfaces frozen in the virtual velocity in non-ideal flows

sources.version: Published version; title, authors, DOI and journal checked on first page

text_evidence_sources: Main-paper and appendix equations and captions

claims.claim: A smooth compatible virtual velocity preserves vorticity transport and vortex-surface tangency.
claims.boundary: Sufficient conditions; global existence in arbitrary 3D flow unresolved. Separate proof supplement not audited.

claims.claim: The artificial normal-force modified flow is dissipative but prohibits the demonstrated reconnection.
claims.boundary: Changing the force changes physical dynamics; finite grid does not resolve the shrinking gap.

claims.claim: Small tangency error does not guarantee a coherent surface history.
claims.boundary: Special exact-geometry negative control, not proof all MHD deformation is spurious.

claims.claim: Approximate virtual transport improves pre-reconnection flux conservation.
claims.boundary: Low-Re symmetric case, omitted gauge and viscosity, null regularization.

claims.claim: Universal smooth virtual tracking through arbitrary reconnection is not established.
claims.boundary: Explicit unresolved existence and singularity problems.
